Independent prototype · DATA steps, MERGE, macros & PROC SORT · Results have not been certified against SAS

What this version supports

Write DATA steps against datasets in the WORK library. Dataset and variable names are case-insensitive. Every statement ends with a semicolon.

Statements

DATA, one SET per step, assignments, subsetting IF, IF / THEN / ELSE, DO / END, indexed DO i = 1 TO 10 BY 2, DELETE, STOP, OUTPUT (including named outputs), KEEP, DROP, RETAIN, sum statements (total + amount;), character LENGTH, and basic FORMAT.

BY groups

BY supports already-sorted data, including multiple keys and per-variable DESCENDING. Use FIRST.variable and LAST.variable. Unsorted input produces an error. PROC SORT can prepare it.

Functions & expressions

SUM MEAN MIN MAX ABS SQRT ROUND CEIL FLOOR INT MOD MISSING N NMISS COALESCE COALESCEC UPCASE LOWCASE STRIP TRIM LEFT LENGTH LENGTHN SUBSTR INDEX CATS CATX TODAY MDY YEAR MONTH DAY

Arithmetic, comparisons (including EQ NE GT GE LT LE), AND OR NOT, IN (…), ||, missing numeric ., _N_, and dates such as '01JAN2026'd.

Formats & CSV

DATE9., YYMMDD10., COMMA12.2, DOLLAR12.2, PERCENT8.1, and basic BEST12. change the result display. Export contains raw values, including numeric SAS dates. CSV types are inferred by column; blanks in numeric columns become missing. Headers must be unique SAS variable names.

MERGE

MERGE claims(in=a) providers(in=b); BY provider; supports two or more sorted inputs, unmatched observations, and repeated keys. Repeated groups are paired one observation at a time, with values carried forward when an input group is exhausted. The row count is the largest group count, rather than a Cartesian product.

IN= indicators are available during the step and excluded from output. Copy one into a new variable to save it. Shared columns are overwritten in input order only when that input is actually read. Input KEEP=, DROP=, and RENAME=(old=new) can separate overlapping columns. Character/numeric conflicts fail clearly.

PROC SORT

PROC SORT DATA=claims OUT=sorted; BY provider DESCENDING paid_amount; RUN; sorts by one or more keys. Omit OUT= to replace the input. NODUPKEY keeps the first observation for each complete BY key. Equal keys retain their original order. Numeric missing values sort first in ascending order.

Macros

%LET, &variable and &variable., %MACRO / %MEND, positional and keyword parameters, %IF / %THEN / %ELSE, block or indexed %DO / %END with %TO / %BY, %LOCAL, %GLOBAL, %PUT, integer %EVAL, and %UPCASE. Macro variables resolve in double-quoted strings and remain literal in single-quoted strings.

Use Expanded code to inspect generated statements. Definitions and macro variables reset with each Run. This is a text-generation subset: no macro quoting functions, indirect && references, %SYSFUNC, runtime CALL SYMPUT, dynamic macro names, or full SAS rescanning. Conditions support simple text comparisons and integer expressions; empty operands and advanced macro expressions are unsupported.

Important limits

This is not the SAS runtime. Character variables without LENGTH use flexible strings; numeric/character type coercion, truncation rules, and function edge cases are not fully SAS-compatible. No positional MERGE without BY, arrays, other PROC procedures, INPUT/INFILE, informats, PUT/INPUT functions, output dataset options, variable lists, special missing values, or SAS7BDAT files. Unsupported syntax fails; unsupported semantic edge cases may still differ from SAS.

100,000 rows per dataset; execution and macro expansion are bounded. Character sort order uses Unicode, which can differ from SAS locale or host collation. Datasets and code are kept only in memory. Importing the same dataset name replaces it. Use test data until you have checked your programs against SAS.

Import CSV

Numeric columns are inferred. CSV headers become variable names.
